review.summary:
Phase 11 delivers all eleven new Red Team dataplane 0.93.0 operations and executable current-spec wire bindings for all 47, and the evidence holds up to independent inspection rather than resting on prose.

Functionality: the eleven methods are present with correct verbs, paths, segment composition, typed bodies and typed returns (crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/reports.rs:331-502, scans.rs:96-115, facade.rs:259-274, custom_attack_reports.rs:208-231). PUT/POST writes are built with RawRequest::new, which leaves replay_safe=false (engine.rs:44-65), so none of the six new writes can be retried; CSV download goes through bounded send_bytes with no text decoding or filesystem write; V2 download returns only a typed location. ThreatOverrideItem.threat_override is Nullable<bool> (data.rs:72-75), so true/false/explicit-null are representable and omission is impossible for a typed caller, exactly as the plan requires.

Security: path IDs are UUID-validated before credentials (common.rs:105-111); query options are validated against the pinned vendor query schema before credentials via the generated contract.json (common.rs:6-53); request bodies are schema-validated in prepare_model before token acquisition. Tests prove, per new route, pre-auth rejection of invalid IDs with RemoteOutcome::NotSent and zero provider calls, destination-policy recheck before authentication, cancellation/deadline before and after dispatch with Unknown outcome after dispatch, no replay of transport/http/decode/limit failures under max_retries=5, redacted errors and redacted model Debug (signed URL and filename never appear), and 409 conflict without silent replay (red_team_contracts.rs:2083-2443).

Contract completeness: contract.json and operations.json each carry exactly 47 operations; tools/red_team_dataplane.py --check --require-complete fails unless every operation is implemented with an executable fixture, and wire_bindings (red_team_dataplane.py:525-556) rejects missing, extra, re-routed, renamed, stale-pin or non-dispatching bindings, with those six mutations unit-tested (test_red_team_dataplane.py:112-127). The 56 wire cases are generated from the pinned OpenAPI with AJV, never from Rust models (make-red-team-wire-fixtures.mjs:1-69), and include 9 omitted-optional variants plus explicit false/zero query encodings. The transport double asserts exact method, URL, full query map, exact header name set and values, and exact body. The twelve rejected legacy parameters are derived from the actual public option structs minus the spec's declared parameters and compared with the reviewed disposition set (red_team_dataplane.py:570-584), and each of the twelve has a negative pre-auth test (red_team_contracts.rs:1557-1627). The four response-presence waivers remain exactly four and apply only to response validation; a fifth required field fails closed with a demand for fresh plan review.

Evidence: docs/checks/phase-11.json records all twenty commands from check_phase.py:71-94 at source 365b7d7a with exit 0, and the 1.89.0/1.99.0 reports show real fmt/check/clippy/test/doc execution (164 lib, 25 red-team contract, 21 resource, 10 schema, 1 vendor-model test with 1636 independent cases). The private-material receipt is an actual scan bound to this source (the gate's --check is correctly labeled as freshness-only), and the fresh live receipt keeps all new vendor operations live-unverified, matching docs/RED_TEAM.md and docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md.

Deductions are limited to bookkeeping and hardening: the phase-status entry records no scope rationale for a command set narrower than phase 10's and no limitations array; the per-route vendor schema literals in Rust are not machine-bound to the ledger's recorded schemas; and no test proves end-to-end rejection of a contract-violating response on any vendor route. None of these undermine this phase's acceptance criteria or the integrity of its evidence.

findings.description: The phase 11 entry records neither a check_scope_rationale nor a limitations array, unlike phases 9 (line 1816-1819) and 10 (line 1881). The phase 11 command set in tools/check_phase.py:71-94 is materially narrower than phase 10's (line 95-121): it drops the test_model_generation.py, test_ci.py and test_g10_release.py suites, `generate_models.py --verify-fixtures`, `scripts/check-native-exports.py`, and the gateway feature-set compile, and it compiles/tests only `--no-default-features --features red-team`. That scoping is defensible under the plan's "extend scoped command sets for 9-12", but it is undocumented, so a reader cannot tell which reductions were deliberate. AGENTS.md:5 requires limitations to be recorded in docs/phase-status.json with the phase outcome; the live-unverified status of the eleven new operations currently appears only inside live_evidence (line 2027) and in prose.
findings.required_fix: Add a check_scope_rationale to the phase 11 entry naming the phase-10 commands deliberately not rerun and why they are not relevant to this change, and add a limitations array stating that all eleven new vendor operations are live-unverified and that this gate compiled and tested only the red-team feature set on 1.89.0/1.99.0 x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.

findings.description: Each vendor call site hardcodes its validation root as a string literal (for example "vendor:red-team-dp:0.93.0:get_static_asr_breakdown_v1_report_static__job_id__asr_get:response" here, and the matching :body/:response pair in send_model at lines 421-422, 446-447, 471-472). The generated ledger already records the authoritative requestSchema/responseSchema per operation (tools/red_team_dataplane.py:285-287, surfaced in crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/contract.json), but nothing binds the two: wire_bindings (red_team_dataplane.py:544-555) checks only method, path, native class/member and that the dispatch arm calls the recorded method, and Rust reads only queryKinds/querySchema from contract.json (common.rs:13-27). For the four override routes, whose body and response schemas are identical, a transposed literal is undetectable by any current check; elsewhere it is caught only incidentally when the wrong root happens to reject the positive fixture.
findings.required_fix: Extend tools/red_team_dataplane.py (wire_bindings or a sibling assertion, with a unit test in tools/test_red_team_dataplane.py) to require that each operation's recorded requestSchema and responseSchema literals appear in the body of its bound native method, so a transposed or stale schema root fails the gate.

findings.description: No test proves end-to-end that a contract-violating response is rejected on any of the 47 vendor routes. The only Decode assertion in this file (line 2213) uses non-JSON bytes, which fails before schema validation. Schema enforcement is asserted only by direct validation::parse calls on component roots (lines 1643-1708) and by the generated model corpus, never through send_contract on an operation :response root. Consequently an absent or overly permissive response root on a new route would pass every positive fixture; the plan's "responses are also validated before model decoding" is therefore unproven at the client boundary.
findings.required_fix: Add at least one case per new route (or a representative subset covering AsrResponse, ReportStatusResponse, ReportDownload, RegenerateResponse, ThreatOverrideResponse and JobResponse) where the armed reply is valid JSON that violates the recorded response contract (for example asr: 101 or a missing required field), asserting ErrorKind::Decode with RemoteOutcome::Unknown and no leaked body content.

findings.description: The embedded contract ships method, path, requestSchema, responseSchema and successStatus for all 47 operations, but the Rust deserializer reads only query_kinds and query_schema (common.rs:13-18), so the remaining fields are unused payload in the published crate. In particular successStatus 202 for regenerate is never enforced: send_contract accepts any success status, so a 200 on a 202-declared route, or a 202 on a 200-declared route, decodes silently. The recorded status is exercised only by the positive wire fixture (wire-fixtures.json:2045).
findings.required_fix: Either enforce the recorded successStatus in the vendor dispatch path and assert a mismatching success status is reported, or restrict the embedded contract.json to the fields Rust consumes and keep method/path/schemas/successStatus only in contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/operations.json.

findings.description: call_vendor contains dispatch arms for members that are not vendor operations in the 47-row ledger, namely ("RedTeamClient", "get_management_languages") at line 1975 and ("RedTeamClient", "get_dashboard_overview") at line 1992. No wire fixture references them, so these arms are unreachable in the vendor corpus and could mislead a maintainer into believing those methods carry current-spec fixture coverage.
findings.required_fix: Remove the two unreachable arms from call_vendor, or move them behind an explicit comment stating they are frozen-only methods outside the 47-operation vendor denominator.

findings.description: The phase 11 live evidence points at docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-10.json, a phase-08-named receipt used as phase-11 evidence. The receipt itself is a legitimate fresh execution bound to this source (executedAt 2026-10-18T17:49, sourceUnchanged true), but the filename misstates its owning phase and makes provenance hard to follow alongside the attempt-08/09 records.
findings.required_fix: Name new live receipts for their owning phase (for example docs/checks/phase-11-live-attempt-10.json) and update contracts/live-evidence.json and the phase entry, or record the continuing attempt-numbering convention explicitly in docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-11.json:1-430 records all 20 commands of tools/check_phase.py:71-94 at source_sha256 365b7d7a… with source_unchanged true and every exit_code 0, including red_team_dataplane.py --check --require-complete reporting {"vendorOperations": 47, "implemented": 47} and make-red-team-wire-fixtures.mjs --check reporting {"independentWireCases":56,"operations":47}

docs/checks/phase-11-rust-1.89.0-red-team.json:1-20 and its test output show actual native execution (fmt/check/clippy/test/examples/doc all exit 0) with 164 library tests, 25 red_team_contracts tests, 21 resource tests, 10 schema tests and the 1-test vendor model probe; the 1.99.0 report mirrors it

crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/facade.rs:259-274 implements download_error_logs as a bounded send_bytes with no JSON decoding, and facade.rs:199-221 keeps POST get_quota as the vendor operation separate from the legacy GET get_quota_summary
crates/scm-sdk/src/engine.rs:44-65 shows RawRequest::new defaults replay_safe=false while read() marks safe_read, so the six new PUT/POST writes are structurally non-retryable
crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_contracts.rs:91-165 asserts exact method, URL, full query map, exact header name set and values, exact body and authorization redaction for every armed request

crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_contracts.rs:2043-2068 drives all 56 vendor cases under both response policies, asserting returned values equal the independent fixtures, consuming every fixture and covering exactly 47 operation ids

crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_contracts.rs:2083-2443 covers, for each of the eleven new routes, invalid path IDs pre-auth, cancellation and deadline before and after dispatch, no replay of transport/http/decode/limit failures for the six writes, override counts 0/1/100/101 with true/false/null/missing and closed-object mutations, runtime-profile codepoint bounds 0/1/256/257, CSV empty/non-UTF8/at-limit/over-limit bytes, 409 conflict, unknown ReportState preservation, and destination-policy recheck

tools/make-red-team-wire-fixtures.mjs:1-69 derives every path, query, body and response from the pinned OpenAPI with AJV 2020 and takes only native call names from the ledger, failing on any operation-set difference

tools/red_team_dataplane.py:42-48 and 570-584 derive the twelve rejected legacy parameters from the actual public option structs minus the spec's declared parameters and fail if they differ from the reviewed dispositions; crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_contracts.rs:1557-1627 gives each of the twelve a pre-auth negative test asserting NotSent and zero provider calls

tools/red_team_dataplane.py:489-494 fails closed on any required-field change beyond the four reviewed waiver pointers and on any unclassified schema change class; crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_contracts.rs:1643-1675 proves the four waivers apply only to response validation and that an unwaived required field still fails

contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/model-fixtures.json:64666-64712 contains the independently computed ASR bound cases -1/0/100/101 with matching responseValid expectations, consumed by crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_vendor_models_generated.rs:10-45 under Request, Response and ResponseWithoutDefaults

tools/test_vendor_red_team_plan.py:34-66 recounts 47 operations (36 previous, 11 added, none removed) with the pinned js-yaml 4.3.2 and compares the plan table's eleven route identities with the actual NEW set

docs/checks/phase-11-private-material.json:1-35 is an actual scan receipt bound to source 365b7d7a with zero credential matches, and scripts/check-private-material.py:205-211 correctly labels the gate's --check as freshness-only rather than a rescan

docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-10.json:1-33 and 247-252 record a fresh credentialed run at this source with 17 verified methods, three Red Team 403s and no cleanup needed; docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md:13-21 and docs/RED_TEAM.md:56-57 state the new operations remain live-unverified

contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/wire-fixtures.json contains 9 omitted_optional_parameters cases and 12 explicit false/zero query encodings, substantiating the coverage claim in docs/RED_TEAM.md:50-51
limitations: Read-only review: I could not execute any command, so compiler, test and checker outcomes are assessed from the recorded reports in docs/checks/ rather than reproduced. The reports are internally consistent, bind the reviewed source hash, and contain per-command output, but a fabricated report could not be detected from inside the repository.

I could not recompute SHA-256 values, so the reviewed source fingerprint, the docs/checks/phase-11.json digest given in the prompt, and the ledger's embedded source/test/fixture hashes are taken as recorded.

I did not byte-compare contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/dp-openapi.yaml or openapi.json against the upstream pin, and no network access was used; the pin is assessed through tools/test_vendor_red_team_plan.py and its recorded passing execution.

I inspected a sample of the 1636-case model corpus (ASR, override, runtime-profile and a selection of generated decode arms) rather than every case, and sampled the 13018-node generated graph only through the declarations relevant to the eleven new operations.
Live service acceptance for the eleven new operations is absent by design in this phase; no new vendor route has successful service evidence, so correctness is established offline only.

CHANGELOG, examples and the CI coverage check are phase 12 deliverables under docs/red-team-data-plane-0.93.0-plan.md and were not judged here; likewise all-feature, cross-platform and packaged-consumer qualification is deferred to phase 12, so this gate's compiler evidence covers only the red-team feature set on x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.
